Wedding shuttle bus in Scottsdale: seats, rates and loops

Scottsdale Sprinters runs wedding shuttle buses as chauffeured guest transport: an executive class seating 8 to 56 that moves guests between the hotel districts, the ceremony and the reception on a booked block of hours. Published rates are $145 to $325 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, and 5 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach, so a wedding shuttle starts between $580 and $1,625 before tax with Arizona sales tax of 8% added at checkout. The wedding party rides in a different class, further down. Below: how the shuttle is sized against a guest count, one way against hourly against a loop, and what it works out at per guest.

Last updated: September 17, 2026

What is a wedding shuttle bus in Scottsdale?

A chauffeured executive shuttle, booked for a block of hours to move wedding guests between the places the day happens. The class Scottsdale Sprinters books for it seats 8 to 56 at $145 to $325 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, and it is the same class a corporate shuttle books. "Wedding bus" covers two jobs, and only one of them is a bus. The guest shuttle is the bus-shaped job: a mini bus or a coach with forward-facing seats in rows, moving the people who are not in the wedding party. The wedding party's own ride is a separate booking from a separate class, with its own section below. Nothing here is a seat sale. You reserve the vehicle and the chauffeur for the hours you book, so 24 guests and 29 guests pay the same for the same Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). A wedding shuttle also runs to a schedule somebody has to hold, and a vehicle that stays with you for the booked hours is how it gets held.

How many guests fit on a wedding shuttle bus?

Between 8 and 56 a trip, depending on the unit. Scottsdale Sprinters seats 24 on the Mini Bus (24 Pax), 27 on the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), 29 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and 56 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach; the executive Sprinters under them take 8 to 14. A seated count is a hard number here, because nobody rides standing. Guests in formal wear take the room they take, so a coach that is exactly full on paper is an unpleasant ride home. Bigger than 56 is two vehicles rather than one; there is nothing larger in this fleet. Two units is often the better answer anyway, because two shuttles can leave two hotel districts at once. Ask for both shapes in one quote.

How do you size a guest shuttle against the guest count?

Count the guests who actually need the ride, not the guest list. Scottsdale Sprinters sizes from the riders staying in one hotel district, then takes the smallest unit that clears them, in seat order: the Mini Bus (24 Pax), the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), then the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Local guests drive themselves; the out-of-town guests are the shuttle list, and in practice that is the room block — a number the couple can count instead of guess. Then choose between a wave and a loop. A wave is everyone at once and needs a unit that seats the whole list. A loop is one vehicle running the same leg repeatedly across the arrival window, trading a smaller vehicle for a longer booking — often for less, because the hours are what you pay for and the seats are not. Geography decides the rest. Old Town Scottsdale, North Scottsdale and Paradise Valley are three different drives, and a room block split across two of them is two pickups rather than one. Say which districts the rooms are in and the quote is written against those addresses.

What does the wedding party ride in?

A different class, booked separately. Scottsdale Sprinters puts the wedding party in the celebration units — the party Sprinters, the Party Bus (28 Pax) and the Pink Hummer Limo — which seat 13 to 28 at $175 to $295 per hour on a 4-hour minimum. They are not guest shuttles and are not sold as one. The difference is the cabin. A celebration unit has lounge seating around the walls, which is a room that moves; a guest shuttle has forward-facing seats in rows, which is how 29 people get somewhere on time. Two bookings, one quote request. The wedding-party ride is usually a short window — the ride in and the ride out — while the guest shuttle is a longer block, and sending both together is how the two timings get checked against each other. Both classes carry the same 4-hour minimum. What this page will not do is put a lounge cabin on the guest-shuttle job; the celebration guides linked below are where those units belong.

One way, hourly or a loop: which shape do you book?

Three shapes. Hourly is the vehicle staying with you for a booked block, on a 4-hour minimum and 5 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. A loop is that same booking spent running one leg repeatedly. A single one-way move is a transfer instead: $295 in an Executive Black Sprinter, $550 in the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). A transfer is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off; longer transfers are priced from the drive with the empty return included. That is the whole rule, and it is why a desert venue prices differently from one a few streets from the rooms. Most weddings book hourly, because most weddings need the vehicle more than once. A transfer is one movement with nothing waiting, so the moment the shuttle has to be back for the return, one hourly block usually beats two transfers on both price and paperwork. The written quote prices both shapes. The loop is what saves money on a long guest list. One Mini Bus (24 Pax) at $185 per hour, running the rooms-to-venue leg repeatedly, moves more guests than its 24 seats and starts at $740 before tax — against $1,625 for a 56-Passenger Motorcoach in one wave.

What does a wedding bus cost per guest?

Divide the booking by the seats. At the minimum, Scottsdale Sprinters shuttles start at $580 to $1,625 before tax, and across the class that splits $29 to $131 a head — the coaches at the bottom, the small executive Sprinters at the top. It is splitting arithmetic, not a per-seat price. The three units a wedding guest list usually lands on sit close together: about $31 a head on the Mini Bus (24 Pax), $31 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and $29 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach, each at its own minimum and across every seat. The figure falls as the vehicle fills, because the fare belongs to the vehicle. The table above prices every unit the same way: published hourly rate, that vehicle's own minimum, the pre-tax total and the total across every seat. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout, a 50% deposit confirms the date, and the balance is charged to the card on file 48 hours before pickup. Two shuttles can beat one: two Mini Bus (24 Pax) units start at $740 each, against $1,625 for one 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Request a current quote against your own addresses.

What are the house rules on a wedding shuttle?

Three carry a fee: $1,500 for smoking or vaping on board, because the smell does not leave, $450 to deep-clean an excessive spill and $450 for a biohazard clean. An added stop on a transfer is $50, and nothing else is added to the base fare. Scottsdale Sprinters publishes the full list on the ride rules page. Arizona's rules for alcohol in a chauffeured vehicle are not ours to summarise loosely, so they have their own page: the Arizona alcohol law guide linked below answers that question, and it applies to a wedding shuttle exactly as it applies to a celebration unit. The rest is what a wedding day needs anyway. Aisles, doors and exits stay clear, which matters more in formal wear than it sounds; one person holds the manifest, so who is still at the rooms has an answer; and the schedule runs through one named contact rather than whoever is nearest the door.

How does the written quote work?

Four steps: pick the unit from the table, send the date with every movement on it, confirm with a 50% deposit, and the balance is charged to the card on file 48 hours before pickup. Every figure on this page is the published rate card; your own total comes back in writing. A quote needs the date and the ready time for each movement, the pickup and final drop addresses, the stops between them, the guest count, and how many hours you want the vehicle. If the day has a guest shuttle and a separate ride for the wedding party, describe both. Call or text (623) 986-6339, email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com, or request a current quote on the pricing page. Name the unit if you know which one you want; the quote confirms it by name, with its rate and its minimum.

Frequently asked questions

How much does a wedding bus rental cost?

Scottsdale Sprinters publishes shuttle rates of $145 to $325 per hour on a 4-hour minimum. The 56-Passenger Motorcoach carries its own 5-hour minimum, so a wedding bus starts between $580 and $1,625 before tax. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout. Request a current quote for your own date and addresses.

How many guests fit on a wedding shuttle bus?

Scottsdale Sprinters seats 8 to 56 across the shuttle class: 24 on the Mini Bus (24 Pax), 27 on the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), 29 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and 56 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Every count is a seated count — nobody rides standing.

What is bridal party transportation, and is it the guest shuttle?

No — Scottsdale Sprinters books them as two different vehicles. Bridal party transportation is the celebration class, seating 13 to 28 at $175 to $295 per hour; the guest shuttle is an executive unit with forward-facing rows. Send both on one quote request.

Can you book a party bus for a wedding?

Yes, for the wedding party. Scottsdale Sprinters books the Party Bus (28 Pax) at $250 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, and it is a lounge cabin rather than rows of seats. For moving guests between the rooms and the venue, the executive shuttles above are the vehicle.

Do you handle wedding transportation in Phoenix as well as Scottsdale?

Yes. Scottsdale Sprinters runs one reservations desk for the whole metro, and the same shuttles, rates and minimums apply — $145 to $325 per hour on a 4-hour minimum. What changes is the itinerary, which is why the quote is written against your own addresses.

Is there an hourly minimum on a wedding bus rental?

Yes. Every Scottsdale Sprinters shuttle books on a 4-hour minimum, so a booking starts at the published rate times that minimum: $580 before tax in an Executive Black Sprinter, $900 in the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). The 56-Passenger Motorcoach is the one exception, on its own 5-hour minimum. A single one-way move books as a transfer instead, with no hour count.

What does a wedding shuttle bus cost per guest?

At the minimum and across every seat, Scottsdale Sprinters shuttles split $29 to $131 a head: about $29 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach and $31 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). You reserve the vehicle rather than the seat, so a half-full shuttle costs the same and the per-head figure rises.

How do shuttle buses for weddings handle more than one hotel?

Scottsdale Sprinters either runs one vehicle on a loop between the two districts or books a second shuttle so both leave at once. Two Mini Bus (24 Pax) units start at $740 each, against $1,625 for one 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Give both addresses and the written quote compares the shapes.

How do I book a wedding shuttle bus in Scottsdale?

Request a current quote with your date and every movement on the pricing page, or call or text Scottsdale Sprinters on (623) 986-6339. A 50% deposit confirms the vehicle and the balance is charged to the card on file 48 hours before pickup.
